content.text: In regions where platforms like Stripe and PayPal are inaccessible, digital creators face significant barriers to launching their stores. Without the right infrastructure, accepting crypto payments and managing orders can feel impossible. This guide outlines how to leverage [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-supabase-order-database-digital-stores-works-how-7|COREMERCH guide to supabase]]-order-database-digital-stores-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-selling-ebooks-nigeria-4|Everything You]]-you-need-9|supabase]] as your order database, ensuring that you can operate independently and efficiently. Whether you're in Nigeria, Venezuela, or another country facing financial isolation, you can set up your digital store without reliance on conventional payment platforms.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

This infrastructure thrives where traditional platforms falter. Platforms like Stripe often exclude many creators based on geography or regulatory hurdles. By utilizing a stack that combines GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, Supabase, and NOWPayments, you create a robust solution tailored for digital creators in these regions. You maintain control over your data, ensuring that every transaction is secure and efficient. Unlike conventional platforms, you’re not dependent on a single provider, thus mitigating risks associated with payment rejections and currency instability.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before embarking on your deployment journey, ensure you have the necessary prerequisites. You’ll need a GitHub or Cloudflare account for hosting, a Google account for Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers, and a NOWPayments account to handle crypto transactions. Additionally, familiarize yourself with Supabase for your order database. Understanding these components is crucial, as they will form the backbone of your digital store, allowing you to easily manage product listings and handle payments securely.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Begin by configuring your backend with either GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting. For Stack 01, deploy using GitHub Pages and Apps Script. Alternatively, for Stack 02, utilize Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Supabase. After setting up your backend, integrate NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment processing. Create webhooks to manage payment notifications and order fulfillment seamlessly. This setup ensures that once a customer makes a purchase, they receive their product instantly, enhancing user experience and satisfaction.
Own your infrastructure and eliminate reliance on traditional payment platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After configuring your infrastructure, it’s time to go live. Test your entire system on the mainnet to ensure everything is functioning as expected. Once verified, promote your store to attract customers. Make sure your payment integration is smooth, and monitor transactions closely. The first transaction is crucial; it serves as a litmus test for your setup. Ensure that your product delivery is prompt and that you have support ready in case of any issues. This proactive approach helps establish trust with your customers.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your store is operational, consider strategies for scaling your digital business. Analyze customer data to understand purchasing patterns and optimize your offerings accordingly. Explore additional integrations or automated tools that can streamline operations further. With the Edge Commerce Stack, you have the flexibility to add more products and configurations as needed. Leverage your full ownership of the infrastructure to innovate and expand without the fear of platform restrictions or fees.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Automate your payment processing for seamless customer transactions.

Your Deployment Checklist

Read the Sovereign Blueprint before you start configuring anything — understanding the complete architecture before touching any settings prevents the most common configuration mistakes. Create all required accounts first: NOWPayments, Cloudflare or GitHub, Supabase or Google account, Resend or Gmail. Then configure the backend with all credentials before deploying it. Then deploy the backend and confirm the endpoint is live. Then configure NOWPayments with the endpoint URL. Then build and deploy the storefront. Then configure your custom domain if using one. Then run the mainnet test. Then check the order database. Then — and only then — share the URL. The sequence is not arbitrary. Each step depends on the previous one.

Can I host a digital product store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages?

Yes, both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages are excellent options for hosting a digital product store. They provide the infrastructure needed to deploy your store and handle crypto payments efficiently.
What products can I sell through this setup?
You can sell a variety of digital products, including ebooks, courses, templates, and software. The infrastructure supports any digital product delivery, ensuring a seamless customer experience.

Utilize NOWPayments for crypto transactions, as it provides automatic payment verification with robust security measures. Regularly test your payment system on the mainnet to identify any vulnerabilities.
